carried_from: data/y-genesis-navigation-v1.js · color_contract · generated 2026-07-18, a presentation fixture whose roles v1 carried forward; v1's three roles are carried forward again here and two are added

who_decided_what.the_ledger: Exodus names the materials — tekhelet, argaman, tola'at shani, shesh — and gold beside them, over and over, and never once says what any of them looked like.
who_decided_what.the_owner: Which material carries which channel, ruled on 2026-09-10. Gold is not a final color: it is an in-process color — huds, boxes, the frame — the way the gold in the tabernacle was worked into the blue that is actually shown. That leaves purple for this project's own voice.
who_decided_what.this_page: Every hex value below, and every one before it. A role is recorded; a hex is a tradition, and the traditions disagree. No reader should come away thinking a hex code is attested — only that a channel was assigned, by a person, on a date.

channels.rule: A channel is not a decoration. It says who is speaking. The corpus speaks in tola'at shani, its reading speaks in tekhelet, this project speaks in argaman, and gold is only ever the frame around one of them.

text_as_written.carries: The Hebrew of the corpus, the letters as the source has them. Carried as a wash behind the letters and not in them: since 2026-09-10 every glyph on this page is argaman, and the ink says nothing about whose words these are.
text_as_written.how_it_is_carried: A wash the width of the word, under the glyph. It lifts while the reader is holding the word and comes back when they let go.
text_as_written.reads_as: a wash behind the letters, and where the eye comes to rest

reading_as_shown.carries: The reading offered for a word: the English that comes from a dictionary this project holds a license to. Someone else's words about the corpus. Carried as a wash, the same as the corpus's own channel, because both are provenance and neither is ink.
reading_as_shown.note: Named and deliberately unused until today. v1 recorded that keeping it unused meant the day it appeared would be a decision somebody made rather than a color that crept in. This is that day, and the decision is recorded above.
reading_as_shown.how_it_is_carried: A wash behind the reading in a book. On the door, where a whole card IS one book's reading, the card carries it and the reading inside is not washed twice.
reading_as_shown.reads_as: a wash behind the reading, and where the eye comes to rest

our_own_voice.carries: Sentences this project wrote: rule statements, counting notes, captions, obligation lines, what a demonstration says about itself, and every line saying a record holds nothing here. This is the page's INK — all of it — so our voice is the unmarked case and everything a reader sees marked is a departure from us into someone else's words.
our_own_voice.why: The owner's ruling. Once red is the text and blue is the reading, the project's own prose is the one voice left without a material, and it is the voice a reader most needs to be able to tell apart from the other two.
our_own_voice.how_it_is_carried: The ink, everywhere, at the neutral weight. The saturated argaman is kept for the narrow case where the page says something is absent, withheld, refused, or does not reconcile.
our_own_voice.reads_as: the ink itself — every glyph on the page is this

structure.carries: The spine: titles, coordinates, the names of parts and chapters. The frame a reading sits in.
structure.in_process: Gold never terminates. It is the box, never the thing in the box, and a word is never left gold — it resolves into a text color or a reading color.
structure.reads_as: line work only: rules, borders, boxes, never ink at rest

reader_selection.carries: What this reader has opened, chosen, pressed or armed among the page's own controls: the verse number the address names, the mode pressed, the chapter opened. Nothing wears it at rest, and no word wears it at all.
reader_selection.in_process: A selection is the most in-process thing on the page, so the page's own controls take gold at its amber value while the reader is pressing them. Words are not controls: what a reader sees under a held word is the word's own channel, weighted, never gold.
reader_selection.held_apart_from_structure_by: Value and behavior, not hue. Structure is gold and does not move. Selection is amber, and it is the only thing on the page that appears and disappears under the reader's hand.
reader_selection.moved_from: v1 valued this electric_blue. Blue is now the reading, so a blue selection would have made the page say 'selected' and 'English' in one color. The collision was reported and this is how it was resolved.
reader_selection.reads_as: ink on the page's own controls under the reader's hand, and gone when they let go; a held word shows no amber, only its own wash deepened
reader_selection.held_word: A word the reader is holding does not take this color. It keeps its ink and deepens its own wash: the same shani under the Hebrew and the same tekhelet under its reading, more of it, and back to resting weight when the reader lets go. The owner, 2026-09-11: "move away from gold as the highlighting itself and move toward just a more opaque red and blue." The thread that runs from a held word to its card leaves in shani and arrives in gold, so it says whose it is at both ends.

faces.rule: One face. The courtyard: linen hangings in daylight. There is nothing here for a reader to choose and nothing kept on the device.
faces.what_was_dropped: The tent's dark face, a purple ground under its coverings, which v1 and v2 both carried and this edition served until today. The owner dropped it. It is not deprecated or left behind a flag: the palette, the toggle, the stored preference and every rule written for it are gone, because a half-removed face paints some elements from a palette nothing else uses, and that is worse than either state.
faces.what_this_costs: A reader whose device is set to dark now gets linen. color-scheme is declared light so the browser does not hand its own dark chrome to a light page. Nothing about the channels moved: they were tuned on this face, and this is the face that was called right.
faces.note: The two-faced rule read: 'the courtyard hangings are linen in daylight, and the tent is dark under its coverings.' Half of that sentence described something this edition no longer does, so the sentence went rather than being left standing over an absence.

note: Linen is not glare: the day ground sits below paper white and its ink is warm, not black. Shesh is the cloth the whole page is written in, which is why it is the neutral and not a channel.
what_changed_after_v2_was_written: [object Object] On 2026-09-11 the held word stopped taking amber: it deepens its own wash instead (channels.reader_selection.held_word), and amber stays with the page's own controls.
